subject: math

objective.text: Split rectangles and circles into thirds and fourths. Name and count the parts.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: Partition circles and rectangles into equal parts, and describe those parts as halves, thirds, or fourths.

explanations.title: Thirds
explanations.text: Thirds means 3 equal shares. Thirds can look long and thin, or short and wide. Each is still 1 third.

explanations.title: More parts, smaller parts
explanations.text: Cut the same rectangle into halves and into thirds. Thirds have more parts. But each part is smaller.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 1: halves vs thirds

explanations.title: Fourths
explanations.text: Fold a circle in half, then in half again. Now there are 4 equal parts. They are fourths, or quarters.

explanations.title: Sharing food
explanations.text: We cut cakes and pizza to share. 3 friends share a pizza equally. Each gets 1 third.

examples.title: Counting fourths
examples.text: Point and count: 1 fourth, 2 fourths, 3 fourths, 4 fourths. 4 fourths is the whole circle.
